binders: A real universal comparison constant C, existentially quantified before all other objects.
An arbitrary type Ω equipped with a measurable space, an arbitrary measure μ on Ω that is a probability measure, an arbitrary function X : Ω → ℝ, and an arbitrary real exponent α.
Two arbitrary property kinds i and j among tail decay, moment growth, absolute MGF, and one-point exponential moment.
An arbitrary input scale Ki and an existentially produced output scale Kj.
hypotheses: The transformed variable Y = |X|^α satisfies property kind i at scale Ki; by definition this premise also includes α > 0 and the measurability, integrability, and inequality requirements specific to kind i.
conclusions: There exists a positive real Kj with Kj ≤ C Ki such that Y = |X|^α satisfies property kind j at scale Kj.
The same C works simultaneously for all probability spaces, probability measures, functions X, positive real exponents α, ordered pairs of the four property formulations, and positive input scales.
mathematical_definitions: Tail property at scale K: Y is measurable, K > 0, and for every t ≥ 0, μ{|Y| ≥ t} ≤ 2 exp(-t/K), with μ of the event converted to a real number.
Moment property at scale K: Y is measurable, K > 0, Y is almost-everywhere measurable, and for every real p ≥ 1, |Y|^p is integrable and E|Y|^p ≤ (Kp)^p.
Absolute-MGF property at scale K: Y is measurable, K > 0, and for every 0 ≤ λ ≤ 1/K, exp(λ|Y|) is integrable and E exp(λ|Y|) ≤ exp(Kλ).
One-point exponential-moment property at scale K: Y is measurable, K > 0, exp(|Y|/K) is integrable, and E exp(|Y|/K) ≤ 2.
The transformed-variable property at exponent α and kind i is the conjunction α > 0 with the corresponding property above for Y(ω)=|X(ω)|^α.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is an absolute real constant C ≥ 1 such that, on every probability space and for every real-valued function X and every α > 0, each of four quantitative descriptions of exponential-type control for the transformed variable |X|^α implies every other one after increasing the positive scale by at most the factor C. Concretely, the four descriptions are exponential tail decay, linear-in-p moment growth, a small-parameter bound for the moment generating function of the absolute value, and a one-point exponential-moment bound; the single C is uniform over the space, measure, X, α, the source and target descriptions, and the starting scale.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The measure must be a probability measure, the exponent α must be strictly positive, and both input and output scales must be strictly positive.

The assertion is an implication from an already-satisfied property at the specified Ki; it does not assert that an arbitrary X has any of the four properties, so an individual implication is vacuous when its premise fails.

The function X is not assumed measurable at the outermost level, but every concrete premise property requires measurability of |X|^α, and the conclusion produces the corresponding measurability requirement for the target property.
The moment quantifier ranges over real p ≥ 1 and uses real powers, not merely integer moments.

The scale K controls the four properties of Y=|X|^α directly; the proposition does not state a norm or scale for X before this power transformation and does not claim optimality or equality of the best constants.
The tail probability uses the real conversion of the measure value; finiteness is ensured here by the probability-measure assumption.
The explicit hypothesis α > 0 is duplicated inside each transformed-variable property, but this duplication does not strengthen the conclusion beyond positivity of α.
ambiguities: The property-kind and declaration names are anonymized, so the descriptive labels tail, moment, absolute-MGF, and one-point are inferred solely from their displayed definition bodies and constructor-to-branch order.

No source context is available to determine whether the intended informal scale parameter for the original variable X should be K, K^(1/α), or another reparameterization; the formal proposition unambiguously compares the displayed K attached to |X|^α.
